title: Group completion of an integral monoid sharpening
statement: Let $P$ be an integral commutative monoid, written additively, where integral means that the canonical map to its group completion $G=P^{\rm gp}$ is injective [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Regard $P$ as a submonoid of $G$, put $U=P^\times=\{u\in P:-u\in P\}$, and let $q:P\to B=P/U$ identify elements differing by addition of a unit [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. Then $U$ is a subgroup of $G$, and $q(p)\mapsto p+U$ defines an injective monoid homomorphism $B\to G/U$. In particular $B$ is integral. For $H=B^{\rm gp}$ the homomorphism $\pi:G\to H$, $p-p'\mapsto q(p)-q(p')$, is surjective and has $\ker\pi=U$. If $a_1,\ldots,a_d$ generate $P$ as a monoid, then $q(a_1),\ldots,q(a_d)$ generate $B$ as a monoid and their images generate $H$ as an abelian group.

proof.text: Work in multiplicative notation. Let f:Pˣ→G be the canonical group homomorphism obtained by composing Units.coeHom with GrothendieckGroup.of, and put U=f.range. This is a subgroup by the group-homomorphism range construction; its carrier is exactly of applied to the unit elements, by unpacking IsUnit.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.1.1--3.1.2, printed p.98, and 3.1.11, p.100; explicit agent algebraic refinement of sharpening and group completion.

proof.text: Let q:G→G/U be the quotient homomorphism. Each of(v) for a unit v lies in U, hence q(of(v))=1. Quotient.liftOn therefore descends p↦q(of(p)) to a monoid homomorphism i:Associates P→G/U. If two images agree, QuotientGroup.mk'_eq_mk' supplies g in U with of(p)g=of(p'). Write g=of(v) for a unit v; injectivity of of gives pv=p', which is exactly the Associates equivalence. Thus i is injective.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.1.1--3.1.2, printed p.98, and 3.1.11, p.100; explicit agent algebraic refinement of sharpening and group completion.

proof.text: Extend i to the group completion by GrothendieckGroup.lift. Its composite with the canonical inclusion is i, by the inverse equations of the lift equivalence. Equality of two canonical images therefore implies equality under i and hence equality in Associates P. Thus the sharpening is integral, without requiring a separate cancellation instance.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.1.1--3.1.2, printed p.98, and 3.1.11, p.100; explicit agent algebraic refinement of sharpening and group completion.

proof.text: Put π=lift(of.comp Associates.mkMonoidHom). Every element in a Grothendieck group is of(a)/of(b), as follows directly by Localization.ind and mk_div_mk. Lift the two Associates representatives to P to prove π surjective. On a fraction of(p)/of(p'), lift(i)∘π equals q, by the lift equations and homomorphism division laws. Thus π(g)=1 implies q(g)=1 and g∈U. Conversely a unit v has Associates.mk(v)=1, hence π(of(v))=1. Therefore ker π=U.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.1.1--3.1.2, printed p.98, and 3.1.11, p.100; explicit agent algebraic refinement of sharpening and group completion.

proof.text: For the specified generating function a, use Submonoid.closure_induction on a representative p∈closure(range a) to show that Associates.mk(p) belongs to the closure of the quotient generators. The induction checks a generator, the identity and multiplication. A second closure induction shows that the canonical image of every b in Associates P belongs to the subgroup generated by the images of these generators. Express any completion element as a quotient of two canonical images and use subgroup closure under division. This includes d=0, since both closure inductions still apply.

lean.statement: theorem integral_sharpening_group_exactness (P : Type u) [CommMonoid P] (hP : Function.Injective (Algebra.GrothendieckGroup.of (M := P))) : ∃ U : Subgroup (Algebra.GrothendieckGroup P), (U : Set (Algebra.GrothendieckGroup P)) = Algebra.GrothendieckGroup.of '' {p : P | IsUnit p} ∧ (∃ i : Associates P →* (Algebra.GrothendieckGroup P ⧸ U), (∀ p : P, i (Associates.mk p) = QuotientGroup.mk' U (Algebra.GrothendieckGroup.of p)) ∧ Function.Injective i) ∧ Function.Injective (Algebra.GrothendieckGroup.of (M := Associates P)) ∧ Function.Surjective (Algebra.GrothendieckGroup.lift (Algebra.GrothendieckGroup.of.comp (Associates.mkMonoidHom : P →* Associates P))) ∧ (Algebra.GrothendieckGroup.lift (Algebra.GrothendieckGroup.of.comp (Associates.mkMonoidHom : P →* Associates P))).ker = U ∧ (∀ (d : ℕ) (a : Fin d → P), Submonoid.closure (Set.range a) = ⊤ → Submonoid.closure (Set.range (fun k ↦ Associates.mk (a k))) = ⊤ ∧ Subgroup.closure (Set.range (fun k ↦ Algebra.GrothendieckGroup.of (Associates.mk (a k)))) = ⊤)
